narrative.overview:
An industrial optical monograph: wide, compactly spaced typography, deep-navy fields, cool paper, and a vivid red signal. Software evidence appears in generous editorial compositions, with hairline divisions rather than enclosing cards. A separate photographic archive extends that identity through full-ratio prints and quiet gallery controls.

Depth belongs to the objects and screenshots. Motion reveals the construction of a camera lens through native scrolling; it remains optional, and the static experience retains readable project evidence and contact access.
keyCharacteristics: Wide display typography and restrained utility text.
Flat editorial surfaces with real project screenshots.
A compact optical study within personal context and an upward-angled circuit plane with faint technical vehicle drawings.
Native scrolling, visible focus, and static graphics fallbacks.

rules.name: The Red Signal Rule
rules.body: Use red for deliberate emphasis, interaction feedback, and the contact field; use the darker About red on cool paper.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Anybody carries expressive headings; Instrument Sans carries reading and controls. Retained alternative font assets are inactive, not additional type roles.

rules.name: The Object Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep editorial containers flat; reserve dimensional treatment for screenshot presentation, photographic prints and physical scene geometry.

dos: Do preserve real screenshots and distinct editorial project compositions.
Do keep red focus outlines and controls with the existing interaction heights (44px generally, 36px in the narrowest header).
Do provide the static lens state for reduced motion, effects off, and software rendering.
Do use SVG paths for interface icons and keep circuit details faint and subordinate.
donts: Don't replace this system with generic card grids, decorative pills, glowing gradients, or burgundy page backgrounds.
Don't turn vehicles into click-operated exhibits or replace the homepage’s contextual optical study with the photography archive; keep the archive on its own linked route.
Don't require motion, hover, or graphics to reach factual content.
